title: Wikipedia cross-language comparison pages
description: English Wikipedia's cross-language comparison material: the 'Comparison of programming languages' family (general, syntax, basic instructions, strings, string functions, list comprehension, object-oriented programming, algebraic data types, associative arrays, arrays, type systems, multi-paradigm and functional languages), comparisons of data-serialization formats, document and lightweight markup languages, relational DBMSs, regex engines, parser generators, assemblers, shells, ISAs, VMs, template engines and documentation generators; pairwise comparisons (C# vs Java, Java vs C++, C# vs VB.NET, VB vs VB.NET, Pascal vs C, Pascal vs Delphi, C vs C++ compatibility); the per-language example sections of concept articles (exception-handling syntax, higher-order functions, string interpolation, coroutines, generators, iterators, async/await, null-coalescing and safe-navigation operators, here documents, entry points, option types, tagged unions, enumerations, reflection, mixins, generics, ...); and the language lists and timelines (by type, by generation, timeline, history, JVM/CLI, concurrent, educational, compilers). Every section anchor was checked against the rendered page's heading ids. `languages` lists the catalog ids of languages whose own Wikipedia article is linked from that table/section (or whose sub-section it is), so it is a lower bound for very large tables.
